name: Ultrasound cavitation / body contouring

lead: Ultrasonic cavitation for body contouring uses low-frequency ultrasound intended to create tiny bubbles in subcutaneous fat, which are said to rupture fat cells so the body can clear the contents. Clinics offer it, and consumer devices are discussed on looksmax.org for face and body fat.

The sources reviewed contain no controlled trial of home or facial cavitation for appearance. Registered studies exist of cavitation in central obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome, but results are not given here.

paras: Cavitation in physics means the formation and violent collapse of vapor bubbles in a liquid when local pressure drops. Proponents apply this idea to fat tissue; forum guides say ultrasound makes bubbles that disrupt fat-cell membranes, after which the fat drains via the lymphatic system.
One forum guide lists deafness, blindness, skin damage, asymmetry, burns and thyroid damage as risks of the practice. No regulatory or clinical safety data on home devices appear in the sources.

lead: Ultrasonic cavitation, as used in cosmetic body contouring, refers to devices that deliver low-frequency ultrasound to the skin with the aim of reducing localized subcutaneous fat. In physics, cavitation is the formation and collapse of vapor-filled bubbles in a liquid when the local pressure falls below the liquid's vapor pressure, and it can produce shock waves and high local temperatures [1]. Cosmetic proponents apply the term to ultrasound-induced bubbles in fatty tissue.

On looksmax.org, users have posted long guides on using cavitation devices at home to reduce facial and body fat, along with threads comparing devices and discussing results [2][3]. Posters describe it as spot reduction and some call it a non-invasive route to destroying fat cells, while others recommend professional treatment [3].

The sources reviewed contain no clinical study of cavitation for cosmetic fat reduction. Registered trials exist on cavitation in central obesity, polycystic ovary syndrome and lipedema [4][5][6][7], but their results are not described here.
infobox: Disrupts subcutaneous fat cells for clearance by the body
No published trial identified in sources

paras: Cavitation in physics refers to vapor-bubble formation and collapse driven by pressure changes rather than by heating; collapse can generate shock waves and microjets [1]. Sonochemistry research has long studied acoustic cavitation, in which bubble collapse creates intense local heating [8], and ultrasound cavitation has industrial uses such as food processing [9].
Cosmetic devices apply low-frequency ultrasound over the skin. In forum descriptions, the sound waves create bubbles that break down fat-cell membranes, letting the body remove the fat [2].

A looksmax.org guide presents ultrasonic cavitation as a way to spot-reduce facial fat at home, with the author stating that the guide is hypothetical and not medical advice [2]. Another poster says the method damages fat cells and the body then disposes of the contents, advising against using it on the face; a reply suggests professional treatment and describes it as a permanent hardmaxx option for people already below about 10 percent body fat [3]. Other threads compare devices and discuss combined cavitation with radiofrequency or alternatives such as fat-dissolving injections [10][11].

One forum guide acknowledges that the method carries risks that include skin damage, asymmetry and burns, and lists more serious possibilities such as hearing, vision and thyroid damage, while advising users to do their own research [12]. The sources reviewed contain no regulatory statement or clinical safety study on home cavitation devices.

No studies found. The clinical literature in the sources does not include a published trial of ultrasound cavitation for cosmetic fat reduction. Trials of ultrasound cavitation are registered for abdominal adiposity and hormones in polycystic ovary syndrome, for insulin resistance in central obesity, and for lipedema [4][5][6][7]; the sources reviewed do not report their results. Separately, cryolipolysis, a different technology, has been reviewed in clinical literature.

lore.intro: On looksmax.org cavitation is discussed as a home or clinic method of fat spot reduction, often for hollow cheeks, with posters split on whether it works or is suitable for the face [2][3].

claims.claim: Ultrasonic cavitation can spot-reduce facial fat at home.
It permanently destroys fat cells non-invasively, and is a hardmaxx option for already lean people.
The method has real risks if misused.
